text: Got it — fixing relativedelta's handling of whole-number floats for years/months (they should be treated as ints, e.g. months=1.0 == months=1). ETA ~5 min.
Got it — rrule with count=0 should yield an empty result set (and count() == 0), not one date. ETA ~8 min.
Got it — str(rrule) should emit the "RRULE:" prefix on the rule line (and round-tripping a parsed "RRULE:..." string should preserve it). ETA ~6 min.

Fixed. relativedelta now normalizes whole-number floats for years/months to ints, so relativedelta(months=1.0) behaves exactly like months=1 (and years=1.0 like years=1): datetime(2000,1,1) + relativedelta(months=1.0) -> datetime(2000,2,1). Genuinely fractional values (e.g. months=1.5) still raise the documented ValueError. Full test suite: 1064 passed, 43 skipped.

Fixed. rrule._iter now returns immediately when count <= 0, so rrule(YEARLY, count=0, dtstart=...) yields no occurrences and rr.count() == 0 (also works with cache=True, rruleset, indexing, before/after/between). Full test suite: 1064 passed, 43 skipped.

Fixed. rrule.__str__ now emits the "RRULE:" prefix on the rule line, so str(rrule(YEARLY, count=5, dtstart=datetime(1997,9,2,9,0))) gives "DTSTART:19970902T090000\nRRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;COUNT=5", and parsing a string containing RRULE: and printing it back preserves the prefix. Round-tripping through rrulestr() still works. Full test suite: 1064 passed, 43 skipped.

Got it — fuzzy parsing is mis-reading a stray "p" (in "http://.../p/...") as a PM time marker, corrupting the hour and dropping the token. I'll make the AM/PM marker only apply when it's actually attached to a parsed time. ETA ~10 min.
Got it — parse('2017-07-17 06:15:', fuzzy=True) must not crash with IndexError; the trailing colon should just be skipped. ETA ~12 min (I'm still finishing the fuzzy "p"/AM-PM fix).

Fixed. In fuzzy mode, an AM/PM-like token ('a', 'p', 'am', 'pm') that isn't actually a valid AM/PM marker (no hour parsed yet, or one already set) is no longer silently swallowed — it now falls through to the normal "unrecognized token" skipping logic. parse("http://biz.yahoo.com/ipo/p/600221.html", fuzzy_with_tokens=True) now returns (datetime(2060, 2, 21, 0, 0), ('http://biz.yahoo.com/ipo/p/', '.html')) with hour 0 and the 'p' preserved in the leftover text. Full suite: 1064 passed, 43 skipped.

Fixed. The HH:MM[:SS] branch indexed l[i+1] without checking that a token followed the second colon, so a trailing colon ran off the end of the token list (IndexError, surfaced as ValueError from _parse). It's now guarded, so parse('2017-07-17 06:15:', fuzzy=True) returns datetime(2017, 7, 17, 6, 15) and the stray ':' is just skipped text. Full suite: 1064 passed, 43 skipped.

Fixed. relativedelta.__add__ (and __sub__, which had the same flaw) selected absolute attributes with `other.x or self.x`, so a legitimately-set 0 was treated as "unset" and dropped. They now use an explicit `is not None` check, so relativedelta() + relativedelta(day=0, hour=0) and relativedelta(day=0, hour=0) + relativedelta() both keep day=0, hour=0 (and the same holds for subtraction). Full suite: 1064 passed, 43 skipped.
